author: Arjan
html:
Nice, so basically it does the same as any server-side HTML stripping function, but then in your HTML editor? Weird that this isn't a standard feature within an HTML editor... By the way, it is better to wrap code in both a `pre` and `code` element, like this: `
[the code]
`. In the next version of HTML, HTML5, there will e an element named `blockcode` to do this job. There are also small JavaScripts that can syntaxhighlight the code, if you use a `class`-name to indicate the language.

author: Geoff
html: @Arjan Like TextMate, the e application basically provides you with a the editor (along with a few basic services); most of the power and flexibility comes from the bundles, which you can (as this command illustrates) customize to your heart's content.
